planting.note: Plant grafted container stock in spring in full sun and well-drained, slightly acidic soil, giving it room to develop its dense pyramidal shape over many years.

directions: This selection intensifies the sky-blue needle color that makes Colorado spruce so popular, carrying it on a tighter, denser pyramidal frame than the species while still slowly building into a substantial specimen over decades. New spring growth emerges an even brighter powder blue before settling into its steely summer tone. It prefers cooler climates and can struggle or show winter dieback at the coldest edge of its range, so a somewhat sheltered site is worthwhile in zone 4. Give it full sun and well-drained soil, since both strong light and dry footing keep the blue color intense and the growth habit dense.

common_name: Sparkling Arrow Variegated Weeping Alaska Cedar

planting.note: Plant in spring in rich, well-drained soil in full to mostly sun, siting it where its narrow cascading silhouette can stand alone as a specimen.

directions: A sport of the narrow weeping cultivar 'Green Arrow', this selection carries the same strictly upright trunk and long pendulous branchlets but splashes the foliage with creamy white variegation, giving the whole cascade a sparkling, two-toned effect. The extremely narrow habit makes it one of the most space-efficient conifers available, fitting into tight side yards or narrow beds where a normal cypress would never fit. Because variegated tissue carries less chlorophyll, growth runs a touch slower than the all-green parent, but the tree still eventually reaches a respectable height on a trunk barely wider than a fence post. Grow in full to mostly sun with regular moisture and good drainage, and avoid pruning the leader, since the weeping branch structure develops naturally along the single central stem.

planting.note: Plant grafted plants in spring in full sun and well-drained soil, reserving a small, permanent spot since this witch's-broom selection gains only an inch or two of size most years.

directions: Propagated from a witch's-broom mutation found on a Korean pine, this cultivar packs soft but firm, bluish-green needles into an unusually dense, compact dome that stays small for a lifetime rather than slowly developing into a tree like the species. Short tufted needle clusters bunch tightly around the branch tips, giving the plant a textured, pincushion-like surface that makes it a favorite for collector troughs and miniature conifer gardens. Because growth is so congested, dead interior needles can accumulate and benefit from an occasional gentle grooming to keep air moving through the canopy. Site it in full sun with well-drained soil, where its glacial growth rate will reward patient gardeners for decades.

planting.note: Plant in spring in full sun and well-drained soil in a rock garden or trough where its button-sized mature size will not be overwhelmed by larger neighbors.

directions: Among the smallest named mugo pine selections, this cultivar holds extremely short needles densely packed over a tight, dome-shaped plant that resembles a sea urchin more than a pine. Growth is measured in a fraction of an inch most years, so even decades-old specimens remain small enough for a trough or tight rock garden pocket. Its compact, predictable size makes it useful anywhere a gardener needs permanent structure without the risk of outgrowing the space. Grow in full sun with well-drained soil, and resist the urge to shear it, since its naturally dense habit needs no shaping.

planting.note: Plant in spring in part shade in moist, well-drained soil, since the white new growth colors most intensely out of hot, direct afternoon sun.

directions: This small, irregularly mounding deodar cedar selection puts on a striking show each spring as new growth emerges ivory-white before gradually fading to a soft creamy yellow through summer. Unlike many white-flushed conifers that bleach out in strong sun, it holds its brightest color with a bit of afternoon shade, making it unusually shade-tolerant for a cedar. Its compact, slow-building habit keeps it well within scale for smaller gardens where a full-sized deodar cedar would quickly dominate. Grow in moist, well-drained soil with some afternoon protection from the hottest sun, and expect a long-lived, low-maintenance specimen once established.

planting.note: Plant in spring or fall in rich, well-drained soil in full sun to bright shade, where its tidy globe shape fits well in a container or small bed.

directions: Selected from thousands of seedlings for its refined, dense texture, this hinoki falsecypress cultivar builds a neat, rounded, globe-shaped form from finely layered dark green foliage that emerges a lighter green each spring. It fills out noticeably faster than many miniature conifer selections, reaching a tidy beach-ball size within just a few years rather than taking decades, while still staying proportionate to small gardens and containers. The dense branching needs no shearing to hold its naturally globose outline. Grow in rich, well-drained soil with consistent moisture, in anything from full sun to fairly bright shade, for year-round structure in a tight planting spot.
